name: Quirinius (the governor during the census)
title: Roman governor of Syria
summary: Publius Sulpicius Quirinius was a Roman governor of Syria mentioned in the Bible in connection with the census that brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem. His administration of the census provided the historical backdrop for Jesus' birth in the city of David.

keyEvents.title: The Census under Quirinius
keyEvents.description: Quirinius conducted a census while he was governor of Syria, which led Joseph and Mary to travel to Bethlehem where Jesus was born.

keyEvents.title: Emperor Augustus' Decree
keyEvents.description: The census was ordered by Emperor Augustus and carried out by Quirinius, requiring everyone to travel to their hometown to be registered.
